title: The South Vietnam upwelling in summer 2018
judge: Codex, single judge; procedure in benchmarking/evaluation/CODEX_JUDGE.md

paper.title: Intraseasonal variability of the South Vietnam upwelling, South China Sea: influence of atmospheric forcing and ocean intrinsic variability

period_match.paper_data: ten-member ensemble of a 1 km SYMPHONIE model
period_match.supplied_data: CMOMS model temperature, salinity and velocity
period_match.note: The paper calls 2018 exceptional relative to a 2009-2018 simulation; here it is ranked within 2011-2020 (finding 1).

verdict_labels: not testable with the supplied data

criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: Summer 2018 was a summer of exceptionally strong upwelling in the southern coastal, offshore and Mekong-shelf areas.
criteria.paper_evidence: Full text: 'the summer of 2018 case, which was an exceptionally strong summer of upwelling for the SCU, OFU and MKU'.
criteria.how_to_test: Testable: the June-September upwelling index of each area in 2018 ranked among the summers of 2011-2020. The paper's reference record is 2009-2018.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: 2018 among the two strongest summers for each area)

anchors.0: Not addressed, or given a verdict without executed analysis of the supplied data (for example the paper's own number restated as a result).
anchors.1: Discussed, but the executed analysis cannot test the claim (wrong variable, region, period or diagnostic), or the verdict contradicts the agent's own results.
anchors.2: Tested with an executed diagnostic, but with a material flaw in definition, masking, sampling or statistics, or with a verdict that disagrees with the frozen reference without explanation.
anchors.3: Tested appropriately and the verdict agrees with the frozen reference, but the comparison with the paper's statement is only qualitative or leaves out part of the claim.
anchors.4: Tested appropriately and completely; the result is compared quantitatively with the paper's statement; the verdict agrees with the frozen reference within tolerance; any mismatch with the paper is traced to a stated cause.
anchors.note: Partly testable: a 4 also requires testing every testable part and stating plainly which part the supplied data cannot test and why. Presenting the untestable part as verified caps the score at 2.

criteria.title: Finding 2
criteria.claim: The southern coastal and Mekong-shelf upwelling are induced by the stable northeastward, then eastward, boundary current.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The MKU and SCU are induced by stable ocean dynamics (the northeastward then eastward boundary current) and have very little chaotic variability.'
criteria.how_to_test: Daily upwelling index of the two areas against the strength of the boundary current and eastward jet in June-September 2018.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: correlation sign exact; magnitude +/-0.2)

criteria.title: Finding 3
criteria.claim: The offshore upwelling develops in July along the northern flank of the eastward jet and in August in the area of cyclonic eddies north of the jet.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'In July, OFU mainly develops along the northern flank of the eastward jet. ... In August ... OFU develops mainly in the area of positive wind curl and cyclonic eddies north of the jet.'
criteria.how_to_test: Location of the offshore cold water relative to the jet axis and to cyclonic vorticity in July and in August 2018.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: position relative to the jet exact; association with cyclonic vorticity exact)

criteria.title: Finding 4
criteria.claim: In mid-summer the alongshore current of the jet and eddy dipole prevents the northern coastal upwelling, which develops in early and late summer when the flow is directed offshore.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'a large-scale circulation formed by the eastward jet and eddy dipole is well established with an alongshore current preventing the NCU development ... the NCU is favored (annihilated) by offshore-oriented (alongshore) structures.'
criteria.how_to_test: Daily northern-area upwelling index against alongshore and offshore surface flow in June-September 2018.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: signs exact)

criteria.title: Finding 5
criteria.claim: The intraseasonal variability follows the wind to first order, and ocean intrinsic variability matters most for the offshore and northern areas.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'driven to the first order by the wind variability ... The OIV has a stronger influence on OFU'.
criteria.how_to_test: This needs daily winds and an ensemble of simulations; neither is supplied.

anchors.0: Ignored, or reported as verified or refuted although the supplied data cannot test it.
anchors.2: Recognised as not fully testable, but without naming what is missing, or a weak proxy presented as a real test.
anchors.4: Stated as not testable with the supplied data, naming the missing data or period; any proxy analysis is labelled as a proxy and not used for the verdict.

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: The paper's SST-based upwelling index (reference temperature 29.2 C and threshold 27.6 C in the paper, or values re-derived for CMOMS with justification); the four upwelling areas; the eastward-jet axis.

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: CMOMS versus a 1 km ensemble: one realisation, coarser resolution, different forcing and tides; a different reference record (2011-2020 instead of 2009-2018).

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
